laura: Heads-up — saw a ~32pp drop in prefix cache hit rate after last night's runtime roll (v2.14). Across a 6k req sample hit-rate went 78% -> 46% and p50 token latency +18ms. Not sure if it's kernel selection or keying drift.

sanjay: ugh. timeline? what changed in the deploy?

laura: deploy-bot says runtime v2.14 rolled at 02:13. Changes listed: kernel-picker heuristic tweak (seq_len bias lowered), small tokenizer upgrade (tokenizer v3.1.0), and a system-prompt sanitation change that removes trailing whitespace.

deploy-bot: runtime v2.14 deployed to prod at 2024-11-02T02:13:12Z. Changes: kernel-picker heuristic, tokenizer v3.1.0, system-prompt normalization.

evan: quick scan — the profiler shows KV cache lookup counts are the same, but prefix-match failures spiked. Looks like canonicalization mismatch: we key on serialized prompt + tool fields order. If system prompt trimming changed, keys differ even if logical prompt is same.

dina: do we version tokenizer inside the key? i thought we pinned tokenization fingerprint (vocab hash) but maybe we use the raw tokenids sequence as part of key.

matt: we keep a tokenizer signature in the key, but only major-version. tokenizer v3.1.0 bumped patch; our current signing code uses `version.major_minor` so it should be stable. However tool/function call fields are serialized with map iteration order — we recently changed JSON lib in infra which now orders keys deterministically by hash, not insertion. That can reorder `tools` field and break keys.

laura: reproduction: two identical requests (only difference is system prompt trailing space) produced different cache keys. dump: ```
key A: prompt="Summarize..."|tools=[name:get_price, params:{currency:USD} ]|tok_sig=3.1
key B: prompt="Summarize..."|tools=[name:get_price, params:{currency:USD}]|tok_sig=3.1
```
(look identical but on the wire we saw additional `\n` in system prompt for A).

sanjay: so multiple vectors: tokenizer patch, system whitespace normalization, and the JSON serializer change. Which is dominant?

evan: ranking by delta: serializer order change explains majority of misses for tool-heavy calls (we see 60% of regressed requests include `tools` or `functions`). system prompt whitespace explains a lot for short-chat prompts. tokenizer patch small effect on a/b of token-level canonicalization.

dina: action checklist suggestion: 1) short-term: add a key-normalizer that canonicalizes tool list (sort by name, stable params order) + trim system prompt trailing whitespace at key generation. 2) mid-term: include a tokenizer fingerprint full-semver in key (not just major_minor) and record tokenizer build id. 3) long-term: introduce a key-versioning field so rollbacks / rollforwards can opt into previous key schema.

matt: +1. Also consider making kernel-picker changes backward-compatible: some kernels expect different KV layouts; we should bias kernel-picker by `key_schema_version` so warmup + prefetch logic uses correct kernel path.

laura: implemented a quick key-normalizer prototype (on dev) — sorts tools array by name, stable-serializes params by sorted keys, and strips trailing whitespace from system prompt before hashing. Local replay: hit-rate returned to 76% on sample. Patch: ```
function canonicalize_key(req) {
  let sys = req.system_prompt.replace(/\s+$/,'');
  let tools = req.tools || [];
  tools.sort((a,b)=> a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
  tools = tools.map(t => ({name: t.name, params: stableSerialize(t.params)}));
  return hash([sys, stableSerialize(req.user_prompt), stableSerialize(tools), tokenizer.fingerprint]);
}
```

sanjay: nice. does stableSerialize include deterministic array ordering? because some params contain arrays where order matters. we must only sort map keys, not arrays.

dina: pass note: we need to add unit tests covering tool param shapes and ensure we don't accidentally reorder arrays.

evan: perf note — canonicalization adds ~0.6ms to key-gen CPU. On p99 high-throughput paths that's small compared to token generation. But it improves cache hit rate which saves tens of ms. Good trade.

matt: we also need to update warmup scripts: when key schema changes we should populate both old and new key spaces for a rollout period (double-warmup). That helps avoid cold-start regressions when kernels/serialization change simultaneously.

laura: proposal for rollout plan: - revert nothing yet. - push key-normalizer hotfix to staging and run 24h replay to validate. - update warmup runner to write both key versions during canary. - add telemetry: emit `key_schema_version` tag and `key_diff` counter for misses caused by normalizer vs tokenizer vs whitespace.

dina: add test matrix: serializer lib versions x tokenizer versions x kernel-picker heuristic on small inputs and toolized inputs. run across 5k synthetic prompts.

evan: also found one kernel selection corner: lowering seq_len bias caused some medium-length requests to be routed to a kernel with different KV-layout packing which invalidated inferred warmup prefixes. So kernel-picker should consult `expected_kv_layout` in model metadata and prefer the same layout for warmup traffic.

sanjay: agreed. I'll take the warmup runner changes & telemetry. laura, can you drive the key-normalizer PR? matt/dina please own tests + release gating.

laura: on it. PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4822 (key-normalizer, tests pending). tagging reviewers @matt @dina.

matt: reviewing today. let's try to get staging replay started tonight. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: staging replay job #728 queued for runtime v2.14 + key-normalizer at 2024-11-02T15:00:00Z.
